entries.claim: Delivered the industry's first full-stack quantum computer built with a standard silicon CMOS chip fabrication process — 300 mm wafer technology — installed at the UK NQCC under the Quantum Computing Testbed Programme.
entries.note: Installation fact is corroborated by NQCC's director quote inside the same release and by independent trade press; the performance of the installed system is a separate, unanswered question.

entries.claim: Selected by DARPA to advance to QBI Stage B — one of 11 of the original 18 Stage A companies.
entries.note: Government selection = admitted to deeper evaluation. It is not a validation of the architecture.

entries.claim: Raised over £42M led by Bosch Ventures (with Porsche SE, British Patient Capital); total funding ~£62M.
entries.note: Investor appetite; no bearing on device physics.

entries.claim: Designed and validated integrated circuits operating at deep cryogenic temperatures (tenths of a degree above absolute zero) for qubit control.
entries.note: Cryo-CMOS control is central to the wiring-wall answer; 'validated' here is the company's own word from a funding release.

entries.claim: Demonstrated an 8 µs spin-qubit readout method and exchange control in a 300 mm-fabricated MOS double quantum dot — the basis for two-qubit gates.
entries.note: Company-described results; venue and peer-review status of the underlying papers not confirmed in Genesis.

entries.claim: Selected for the initial phase of DARPA US2QC alongside Atom Computing and Microsoft.
Advanced to US2QC's final validation/co-design phase (= QBI Stage C goals) after a year-long evaluation by a ~50-expert team.
entries.note: The furthest rung any company has reached on the DARPA ladder — and still an evaluation-in-progress, not a passed exam.

entries.claim: Announced Omega: a photonic chipset containing all components needed for million-qubit-scale systems, manufactured at GlobalFoundries.
entries.note: Company framing; the component-level measurements are in the peer-reviewed Nature paper — both are entered as evidence separately.

entries.claim: Signed a $125M expanded QBI agreement with DARPA (following a $31.8M Stage C tasking in Sep 2025).
entries.note: Contract value measures government willingness to pay for evaluation depth — it is not a measurement of qubit performance.

entries.claim: Will break ground in 2025 on datacenter-sized Quantum Compute Centers in Brisbane and Chicago.
entries.note: Forward-looking construction claim; completion status unverified at Genesis close.

entries.claim: Awarded an NQCC/UKRI testbed contract (Silicon Cloverleaf) — one of seven testbeds funded under the £30M programme.
entries.note: A delivery contract with milestones; award ≠ delivered system ≠ validated performance.
